variants.headline: Looking back: a company goes under
variants.sub: The colony has seen the failure of {company}.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: The company {company} had gone under.

Our principles ask how an economy serves the colony, including when an enterprise fails. A business outcome should not make the people around it disappear into a convenient political slogan. Responsibility deserves an argument about stewardship, rather than a ready-made morality tale built from facts that are not known.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We judge {target} critically. Business failure deserves more than a shrug, and the standards of stewardship should be examined rather than dismissed as irrelevant once an enterprise has gone under.

variants.headline: Looking back: an enterprise reaches failure
variants.body:

Responsibility deserves an argument about stewardship, rather than a ready-made morality tale built from facts that are not known.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.
